body.statement:
For every triangular array \((\theta_n)\) with \(\theta_n\in\Theta\), sampled according to the declared independent stratified sampling model, write the observation in environment \(e\) as \(W_{e,i}=(T_{e,i},Y_{e,i})\), put \(C^+=(C^\top C)^{-1}C^\top\), and put \(h_k=m_k-\beta c_k\).  There are centered first-projection arrays \(\psi^C_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\), \(\psi^c_{e,k,n}(W_{e,i})\), and \(\psi^m_{e,k,n}(W_{e,i})\) such that, simultaneously for \(d+2\leq k\leq R_{\max}\),
\[
 \sqrt n\,\widehat Q(\widehat m_k-\beta\widehat c_k)
 =Z_{n,k}+o_{\mathbb P}(1),
 \qquad
 Z_{n,k}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}\pi_e^{-1}\zeta_{e,k,n}(W_{e,i}),
\]
uniformly over all such arrays, where
\[
 \zeta_{e,k,n}
 =Q_A\bigl(\psi^m_{e,k,n}-\beta\psi^c_{e,k,n}
       -\psi^C_{e,n}C^+h_k\bigr).
\]
The remainder is uniform in probability, and the stacked vector \(Z_n=(Z_{n,k}:d+2\leq k\leq R_{\max})\) satisfies
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L(Z_n),N(0,\Sigma_n)\right)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \Sigma_n=\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\pi_e^{-1}
 \mathbb E\bigl[\zeta_{e,n}\zeta_{e,n}^{\top}\bigr],
\]
uniformly over the bounded ambient class.  This conclusion allows \(\Sigma_n\) to be singular; \(N(0,\Sigma_n)\) is then the Gaussian law supported on \(\operatorname{im}(\Sigma_n)\).  The term \(-Q_A\psi^C_{e,n}C^+h_k\) is the same-sample estimated-\(A\) correction.  No breakout, first-breakout order, or lower bound on \(\lVert Q_Ac_k\rVert_2\) is required.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an arbitrary triangular array \((\theta_n)\) in \(\Theta\).  All constants below depend only on the fixed bounds defining \(\Theta\), the balanced-share constants, \(E\), \(d\), and \(R_{\max}\), and hence are uniform over this array.  The declared sampling model gives independence within and across environments and identical distribution with law \(P_e\) within environment \(e\).  By the balanced-share assumption,
\[
 n_e=n\pi_e\geq n\underline\pi . \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(n_e\geq R_{\max}\) in every environment for all sufficiently large \(n\), and the small-sample fallback in the cumulant-SVD definition is eventually inactive.

Set \(s_0=2R_{\max}+\delta\).  The effect, treatment-loading, and confounding bounds imply
\[
 |\alpha|\leq a_1,
 \qquad |\beta|\leq B,
 \qquad |\gamma|=|\alpha|\,|\gamma/\alpha|\leq a_1q_1. \tag{2}
\]
The structural equations in the ambient-class definition give
\[
 T_e=\alpha\epsilon_{u,e}+\epsilon_{t,e},
 \qquad
 Y_e=(\beta\alpha+\gamma)\epsilon_{u,e}
      +\beta\epsilon_{t,e}+\epsilon_y. \tag{3}
\]
For \(s_0>1\), convexity gives
\[
 |x_1+\cdots+x_j|^{s_0}
 \leq j^{s_0-1}\sum_{a=1}^j|x_a|^{s_0}. \tag{4}
\]
Applying (4) to (3), then using (2) and the source moment-envelope assumption, yields a constant \(K_W<\infty\) such that
\[
 \sup_n\max_{e\in\mathcal E}
 \mathbb E_{\theta_n}\|W_{e,1}\|^{2R_{\max}+\delta}
 \leq K_W. \tag{5}
\]
Every moment and cumulant of \((T_e,Y_e)\) through order \(R_{\max}\) is therefore uniformly bounded.  In particular, the finite dimension of the contrast vectors gives uniform bounds on \(C\), \(c_k\), \(m_k\), and \(h_k=m_k-\beta c_k\) for \(2\leq k\leq R_{\max}\).

We next derive the influence representations.  For variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\), the moment--cumulant polynomial is
\[
 \kappa_k(X_1,\ldots,X_k)
 =\sum_{\mathcal P\in\Pi_k}
 (|\mathcal P|-1)!(-1)^{|\mathcal P|-1}
 \prod_{D\in\mathcal P}
 \mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{j\in D}X_j\right], \tag{6}
\]
where \(\Pi_k\) is the finite set of partitions of \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\).  For a partition with \(s\) blocks, average the corresponding block monomials over \(s\) distinct observations and symmetrize.  Its expectation is the product in (6), so the unbiased sample cumulant stipulated in the estimator definition is a fixed finite linear combination of symmetric \(U\)-statistics of orders at most \(k\), with kernels of total degree at most \(k\).

Consider one order-\(s\) constituent \(U_{n_e,s}(g)\).  Successively subtracting conditional expectations produces canonical projections \(g_j\), \(1\leq j\leq s\), and the exact identity
\[
 U_{n_e,s}(g)-\mathbb Eg
 =\frac1{n_e}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}\psi_g(W_{e,i})
  +\sum_{j=2}^s {s\choose j}U_{n_e,j}(g_j), \tag{7}
\]
where
\[
 \psi_g(w)=s\{\mathbb E[g(w,W_2,\ldots,W_s)]-\mathbb Eg\}.
\]
Each \(g_j\) is centered conditionally on any one argument.  In the second moment of \(U_{n_e,j}(g_j)\), two distinct index sets have zero cross expectation whenever their union contains an index belonging to only one set; if the sets are distinct, such an index exists.  Hence only equal index sets contribute and
\[
 \mathbb E\{U_{n_e,j}(g_j)^2\}
 ={n_e\choose j}^{-1}\mathbb E(g_j^2)
 \leq K n_e^{-j}. \tag{8}
\]
The final inequality is uniform because the squared kernels have degree at most \(2R_{\max}\), and (5), conditional Jensen's inequality, and H\"older's inequality bound all their second moments.  Since the numbers of orders, partitions, environments, and coordinates are fixed, the sum of the terms in (7) having projection order at least two is \(O_{L^2}(n_e^{-1})\), uniformly.

Apply the environment-versus-baseline signs in the contrast definitions and stack the corresponding first projections.  This defines centered arrays \(\psi^C_{e,n}\), \(\psi^c_{e,k,n}\), and \(\psi^m_{e,k,n}\).  Equations (1), (7), and (8) give, simultaneously over the finitely many relevant \(k\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n(\widehat C-C)
 &=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
   \pi_e^{-1}\psi^C_{e,n}(W_{e,i})+o_{L^2}(1),\\
 \sqrt n(\widehat c_k-c_k)
 &=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
   \pi_e^{-1}\psi^c_{e,k,n}(W_{e,i})+o_{L^2}(1),\\
 \sqrt n(\widehat m_k-m_k)
 &=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
   \pi_e^{-1}\psi^m_{e,k,n}(W_{e,i})+o_{L^2}(1).
 \end{aligned} \tag{9}
\]
Here uniform \(o_{L^2}(1)\) follows because multiplication of the bound \(O_{L^2}(n_e^{-1})\) by \(\sqrt n\) gives \(O(n^{-1/2})\) under (1).

Put
\[
 \nu=\min\{1,\delta/R_{\max}\}>0. \tag{10}
\]
Each first projection in (9) is a finite sum of polynomials of degree at most \(R_{\max}\) in one observation, with coefficients given by uniformly bounded lower-order moments.  Conditional Jensen's inequality and (5) therefore give
\[
 \sup_{n,e,\theta_n}\mathbb E_{\theta_n}\!\left[
 \|\psi^C_{e,n}\|^{2+\nu}
 +\sum_{k=2}^{R_{\max}}
 \{\|\psi^c_{e,k,n}\|^{2+\nu}
   +\|\psi^m_{e,k,n}\|^{2+\nu}\}
 \right]<\infty, \tag{11}
\]
because \((2+\nu)R_{\max}\leq2R_{\max}+\delta\).

We now linearize the generated projector.  Let \(P_C=CC^+\), where \(C^+=(C^\top C)^{-1}C^\top\); then \(Q_A=I_{E-1}-P_C\).  The calibration-rank and calibration-gap assumptions license the inverse and imply
\[
 \|C^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sigma_d(C)^{-1}\leq\kappa_0^{-1}. \tag{12}
\]
For a perturbation \(H\) with \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa_0/2\), the triangle inequality gives \(\sigma_d(C+H)\geq\kappa_0/2\).  With \(G=C^\top C\) and \(D=C^\top H+H^\top C+H^\top H\), the exact inverse identity
\[
 (G+D)^{-1}=G^{-1}-G^{-1}DG^{-1}
 +G^{-1}DG^{-1}D(G+D)^{-1} \tag{13}
\]
can be substituted into the formula for \(P_{C+H}\).  Collecting the linear terms and bounding every remaining product by (5), (12), and \(\sigma_d(C+H)\geq\kappa_0/2\) gives
\[
 P_{C+H}-P_C
 =Q_AHC^+ +(Q_AHC^+)^\top+R_C(H),
 \qquad \|R_C(H)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq K_P\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2, \tag{14}
\]
with \(K_P\) uniform.

Equation (9) and (11) imply \(\|\widehat C-C\|=O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly.  Taking \(H=\widehat C-C\) in (14), the event on which (14) applies has probability tending to one uniformly, and its remainder is \(O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1})\).  On that event the rank-\(d\) SVD projector is the column-space projector of \(\widehat C\).  Therefore
\[
 \widehat Q-Q_A
 =-Q_A(\widehat C-C)C^+
  -\{Q_A(\widehat C-C)C^+\}^\top
  +o_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}) \tag{15}
\]
uniformly over \(\Theta\).

The established cumulant-cancellation lemma applies to every \(\theta_n\in\Theta\) and gives
\[
 h_k=m_k-\beta c_k=\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k\in A=\operatorname{col}(C),
 \qquad Q_Ah_k=0. \tag{16}
\]
It follows directly that
\[
 \{Q_A(\widehat C-C)C^+\}^\top h_k
 =C^{+\top}(\widehat C-C)^\top Q_Ah_k=0. \tag{17}
\]
Writing \(\widehat h_k=\widehat m_k-\beta\widehat c_k\), equations (9), (12), and (15)--(17) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n\,\widehat Q\widehat h_k
 &=\sqrt n\,Q_A(\widehat h_k-h_k)
   +\sqrt n(\widehat Q-Q_A)h_k
   +\sqrt n(\widehat Q-Q_A)(\widehat h_k-h_k)\\
 &=\sqrt n\,Q_A\{(\widehat m_k-m_k)
       -\beta(\widehat c_k-c_k)\}
   -\sqrt n\,Q_A(\widehat C-C)C^+h_k+o_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \end{aligned} \tag{18}
\]
Indeed, the product in the first line is \(O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2})\) after multiplication by \(\sqrt n\), uniformly.  Substitution of (9) into (18) proves
\[
 \sqrt n\,\widehat Q(\widehat m_k-\beta\widehat c_k)
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
 \pi_e^{-1}\zeta_{e,k,n}(W_{e,i})+o_{\mathbb P}(1), \tag{19}
\]
where
\[
 \zeta_{e,k,n}
 =Q_A\{\psi^m_{e,k,n}-\beta\psi^c_{e,k,n}
       -\psi^C_{e,n}C^+h_k\}. \tag{20}
\]
The finite number of \(k\)'s makes the remainders simultaneous.  Formula (20) proves the asserted estimated-plane correction, including its sign.

It remains to establish the Gaussian approximation without a covariance-rank condition.  Stack (20) over \(d+2\leq k\leq R_{\max}\).  Equations (11), (12), and the uniform bounds on \(h_k\) imply
\[
 \sup_{n,e,\theta_n}\mathbb E_{\theta_n}\|\zeta_{e,n}\|^{2+\nu}<\infty. \tag{21}
\]
For \(a=(e,i)\), put
\[
 X_a=n^{-1/2}\pi_e^{-1}\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i}),
 \qquad L_n=\sum_a\mathbb E\|X_a\|^{2+\nu}.
\]
Then (1) and (21) give
\[
 L_n\leq K n^{-1-\nu/2}\sum_e n_e\pi_e^{-(2+\nu)}
 \leq K'n^{-\nu/2}. \tag{22}
\]
For each \(a\), let \(G_a\) be an independent centered Gaussian vector with the same covariance as \(X_a\).  Fixed-dimensional Gaussian integration and Lyapunov's inequality give
\[
 \mathbb E\|G_a\|^{2+\nu}
 \leq K\{\mathbb E\|X_a\|^2\}^{1+\nu/2}
 \leq K\mathbb E\|X_a\|^{2+\nu}. \tag{23}
\]
To verify the replacement rather than invoke a nonsingular limit theorem, let \(f\) be bounded by one and one-Lipschitz, and convolve it with \(N(0,\varepsilon^2I)\) to obtain \(f_\varepsilon\).  Differentiation under the Gaussian integral gives
\[
 \sup_x\|D^2f_\varepsilon(x)\|\leq K\varepsilon^{-1},
 \qquad
 \sup_x\|D^3f_\varepsilon(x)\|\leq K\varepsilon^{-2}.
\]
Interpolating these two bounds yields
\[
 \|D^2f_\varepsilon(x)-D^2f_\varepsilon(y)\|
 \leq K\varepsilon^{-(1+\nu)}\|x-y\|^\nu. \tag{24}
\]
The integral Taylor remainder is consequently bounded by
\[
 \left|f_\varepsilon(x+v)-f_\varepsilon(x)-Df_\varepsilon(x)v
 -\tfrac12v^\top D^2f_\varepsilon(x)v\right|
 \leq K\varepsilon^{-(1+\nu)}\|v\|^{2+\nu}. \tag{25}
\]
Replacing the \(X_a\)'s successively by the \(G_a\)'s cancels the constant, linear, and quadratic expectations because each pair has equal mass, mean, and covariance.  Equations (23)--(25) therefore give
\[
 \left|\mathbb Ef_\varepsilon\!\left(\sum_aX_a\right)
 -\mathbb Ef_\varepsilon\!\left(\sum_aG_a\right)\right|
 \leq K\varepsilon^{-(1+\nu)}L_n. \tag{26}
\]
Translation coupling also gives \(\|f_\varepsilon-f\|_\infty\leq K\varepsilon\).  Choosing \(\varepsilon=L_n^{1/(2+\nu)}\) when \(L_n>0\), and observing that both sums vanish almost surely when \(L_n=0\), proves from (22)--(26) that
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L\!\left(\sum_aX_a\right),
 \mathcal L\!\left(\sum_aG_a\right)\right)\longrightarrow0 \tag{27}
\]
uniformly.  Finally, stratified independence and \(n_e=n\pi_e\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}\!\left(\sum_aG_a\right)
 =\frac1n\sum_e n_e\pi_e^{-2}
 \mathbb E[\zeta_{e,n}\zeta_{e,n}^\top]
 =\Sigma_n. \tag{28}
\]
Thus the Gaussian sum has law \(N(0,\Sigma_n)\).  The construction is valid for every positive semidefinite \(\Sigma_n\); if it is singular, this Gaussian is supported on its image, and if it is zero, it is the point mass at zero.  Equations (19), (27), and (28) prove the lemma.  No step used \(r\), \(\lambda_n\), a nonzero projected contrast, or a breakout condition.
